summary: The iOS app's landing screen (ConnectionsScreen) now opens with Recents above the machine list, with the rules of native Android's Home (HomePresenter). Recents lists every chat of every paired machine, ranked by what it needs: Approval, then Input or Plan, then Working (with a spinner), Failed, Done (unread) and the rest, each newest first. A row shows the title (Untitled chat when blank), the project and machine name, and the status or, with no status, the relative time. It shows five rows and Show more adds five. A tap opens the chat. A chat's status comes only from this run: live events (the chat store stamps each live status change with a clock, statusAt, never restored from disk) plus the backend's provider:list-sessions reply, asked on every Home visit and on each connect. A thread missing from that reply has no live session, and a live change after the request beats the reply. Attention comes from the chat's feed: a pending approval, an unanswered question, or a plan with no user message after it. Each machine's chat list is kept on the phone (stores/recents.ts, the newest 50 per machine), so an offline machine still lists its chats, with no status; the demo is never written and an unpaired machine's list is dropped. The machine list and its management stay on the same screen: unlike Android, iOS keeps the full list there instead of three rows plus Manage.

desktop.reason: The desktop has no phone Home screen; its sidebar Recents (sidebar-needs-you) is unchanged.

sharedBackendApi.reason: Uses the existing app:get-projects and provider:list-sessions channels unchanged (LiveSessionSummary in src/shared/live-sessions.ts). A backend that fails either call is logged; Recents keeps the last list and shows no reply-based status.

updateRelease.reason: JavaScript only, with no native module, permission or app.json change, so the fingerprint runtimeVersion is unchanged and it ships on the mobile-ota.yml iOS lane. The new AsyncStorage key switchboard-recents starts empty on an upgrade and an older app ignores it. Android is unchanged.

automated: npx vitest run tests/unit/mobile-home-recents.test.ts: the Android HomePresentationTest cases (attention outranks Working, Failed and Done and the route fields are kept; neutral rows newest first; one row per chat per machine but the same id on two machines; a bounded page with its total; answered cards drop attention) plus the status source (a restored status shows nothing, a live status this run shows, the list-sessions reply sets and clears, a live change after the request wins both ways), the disk cap and the relative time
npx vitest run tests/unit/mobile-chat-store.test.ts: each live status change gets a statusAt after the mark taken before it
npx jest (apps/mobile): RecentsList renders the empty copy, title, project and machine, time or status with the Working spinner, opens the chat on tap and offers Show more only while rows remain
npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/mobile and npm run typecheck
notExercised: Not run on an iPhone or a simulator, and not against a live backend.

Threads the desktop started under a synthetic agent_<ts> id while the project list shows the provider's session id match neither live events nor the list-sessions reply, so they show no status, as on Android.
